newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Sept copper cable/wire orders, shipments up.
newsitem.headline: Japan Sept copper cable/wire orders, shipments up.

text.p: Japanese orders and shipments of copper wire and cable in September rose from the same month last year, the Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association said on Friday.
Orders rose 0.2 percent year-on-year to 88,600 tonnes, while shipments were up 2.9 percent at 90,400 tonnes.
On a month-on-month basis, orders rose 10.5 percent from August's upwardly revised 80,174 tonnes, while shipments were up 17.2 percent from August's downwardly revised 77,125 tonnes.
Orders for the first half of the fiscal year beginning April 1996 rose a marginal 0.9 percent from the year-ago period to 513,700 tonnes, while shipments were up 2.0 percent at 512,900 tonnes.

In the September figures, shipments to the construction sector showed continued steady growth, rising 4.3 percent year-on-year to 32,800 tonnes, the eighth consecutive month of gains, while the auto sector showed particularly sharp growth of 20.7 percent to 6,700 tonnes.
Exports continued to decline, as other Asian countries built up their own domestic production capacity, association officials said.
September export shipments were down 11.5 percent year-on-year at 4,700 tonnes while orders fell 6.7 percent to 4,600 tonnes.
One association official added, however, that Japanese cable makers' offshore production facilities in Asia were beginning to contribute to profits.
"They may not yet have gotten to the point where they're finally harvesting the results of their investments, but it seems they have made it past the start-up phase," he said.
A recent survey of profitability at Japan's wire and cable makers found that many Asian operations are now contributing to their Japanese parent's consolidated profits, he said.
